gdp_level.source: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CN · GDP at current prices, rupee million, annual.
gdp_level.description: The total value of everything Pakistan produces in a year, at current prices. Years are Pakistan's fiscal years, July to June, labelled by the year in which they end. Annual only: Pakistan's quarterly national accounts are not available to automated downloads.
gdp_level.real: “Make it real” swaps this to GDP at constant prices (World Bank), also annual. This strips out the effect of price changes, so it shows genuine output growth rather than growth that's really just inflation.
gdp_level.dollar: “Dollarise” converts each year at its own PKR/USD rate (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF, annual average), from 1982.

gdp_real.source: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.KN · GDP at constant prices, rupee million, annual.
gdp_real.description: GDP adjusted for inflation, so changes reflect real output growth rather than price changes.
gdp_real.real: This IS the “Make it real” series, toggling it off shows GDP at current (nominal) prices instead.
gdp_real.dollar: With “Make it real” on, “Dollarise” converts every year at one rate, the average for the latest year, so dollar growth equals real growth.

gdp_growth.source: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.KN · change in real GDP on the previous year, to one decimal place.
gdp_growth.description: How much the economy grew or shrank compared with the previous year, in real terms. Annual only on this page.
gdp_growth.real: This is already a real (inflation-adjusted) growth rate, “Make it real” has no additional effect on it.
gdp_growth.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic, converting the underlying rupees to dollars doesn't change the percentage change. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

cpi.source: IMF consumer price index (CPI, PAK.CPI._T.YOY_PCH_PA_PT.M), from the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics · national CPI, all items, change on the same month a year earlier as the IMF publishes it, to one decimal place, monthly.
cpi.description: How much consumer prices are rising compared with a year ago. This is the national index, a weighted average of the urban and rural indexes, on a 2015-16 base.

cpi_mom.source: IMF consumer price index (CPI, PAK.CPI._T.POP_PCH_PA_PT.M) · national CPI, all items, change on the previous month, not seasonally adjusted, to one decimal place.
cpi_mom.description: How much consumer prices changed in the latest month.

unemployment.source: World Bank SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS · International Labour Organization modelled estimate, % of the labour force, annual, from 2012 (the modelled series reads under 1% before then, far below Pakistan's own surveys).
unemployment.description: The share of the labour force that wants a job and is actively looking, but can't find one. This is the ILO's modelled estimate, not the statistics office's own survey rate.

exports.source: IMF international trade in goods (ITG) · exports of goods, free on board, in rupees as Pakistan reports them, monthly, from July 2022 (the IMF series has no figures for November 2021 to June 2022).
exports.description: The value of goods Pakistan sells to the rest of the world each month, in rupees.
exports.dollar: These figures are reported in rupees; “Dollarise” converts each year at that year's World Bank rate.

imports.source: IMF international trade in goods (ITG) · imports of goods, cost, insurance and freight, in rupees as Pakistan reports them, monthly, from July 2022.
imports.description: The value of goods Pakistan buys from the rest of the world each month, in rupees.
imports.dollar: These figures are reported in rupees; “Dollarise” converts each year at that year's World Bank rate.

trade_balance.source: IMF international trade in goods (ITG) · exports less imports of goods, rupees, monthly, from July 2022.
trade_balance.description: Exports minus imports of goods. A negative number is a trade deficit.
trade_balance.dollar: These figures are reported in rupees; “Dollarise” converts each year at that year's World Bank rate.

debt_gdp.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (GGXWDG_NGDP) · general government gross debt, % of GDP, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
debt_gdp.description: Everything government owes, across all levels of government, compared with the size of the economy.
debt_gdp.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

deficit.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (GGXCNL_NGDP) · general government net lending (+) or borrowing (-), % of GDP, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
deficit.description: The gap between what government takes in and what it spends in a year, across all levels of government. A negative number is a deficit.
deficit.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

current_account.source: World Bank BN.CAB.XOKA.GD.ZS · current account balance, % of GDP, annual.
current_account.description: The balance of trade in goods and services plus income and transfers with the rest of the world. A negative number means the country is borrowing from abroad.
current_account.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

fdi.source: World Bank BX.KLT.DINV.WD.GD.ZS · foreign direct investment, net inflows, % of GDP, annual.
fdi.description: Long-term investment into the country by foreign companies and investors, such as building factories or buying a lasting stake in a business.
fdi.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

fx_usd.source: World Bank series PA.NUS.FCRF · official exchange rate, annual average, shown as US$ per Rs100 (100 ÷ the published PKR per US$), from 1982.
fx_usd.description: How many US dollars Rs100 buy. A rising number means a stronger rupee.
